name: Docker
tagline: Containers, Compose, Engine API, Docker Hub, and CLI workflows.
shortDescription: Docker is highly scriptable through CLI, Compose, Engine API, registries, and local reproducible environments.
agentSummary: Agents can build, run, inspect, test, and compose local services with repeatable commands and logs.
bestFor: Local dev environments, container builds, integration tests, and deployment artifacts.
cautionNotes: Key limitations: Agents need limits around privileged containers, volume mounts, secrets, and registry pushes. Deploys, secret changes, IAM, billing, networking, deletes, and rollback paths have high production blast radius; require scoped credentials and review gates. CLI access is powerful but can run destructive local or production commands; prefer dry runs, preview environments, and non-production credentials. API automation needs client-side throttling, idempotency where supported, pagination limits, retries, and audit logging.
pricingSummary: Public Docker Desktop/Hub/team pricing plus open-source Engine components.
authModel: Local daemon access, Docker Hub tokens, registry credentials, and contexts.
accountCreation: CLI can be local; Docker Hub signup is self-serve.
browserSupport: Desktop and Hub UI help inspect images, repos, and billing.

capabilities.detail: Docker CLI and Compose CLI cover build, run, logs, exec, compose, and registry workflows.
Docker Engine API provides programmatic daemon access.
Docs include CLI, API, Compose, Dockerfile, and security references.
Public Docker Desktop/Hub/team pricing plus open-source Engine components.
CLI can be local; Docker Hub signup is self-serve.
Desktop and Hub UI help inspect images, repos, and billing.
Local containers provide isolated repeatable test environments.
